original_question: Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or to P1 with the compact-open topology, and let U be the subset of maps h such that translates h(z+a_n) can approximate every f in H. What is the minimal possible growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic Th(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(ω) for maps h in U?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.1: the open problem asking for the minimal growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic T_h for translation-universal entire maps h in H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual statement: it identifies the same function space H, the same universal subset U defined through translates h(z+a_n), and the same Nevanlinna characteristic T_h(r). In substance, it is essentially Problem 9.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper treats two separate ambient spaces: H is either the space of entire maps C -> C or, separately, the space of entire maps C -> P^1; it does not fuse these into one mixed space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The translate notation is made explicit in the paper: h_{a_n}(z) := h(z+a_n). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The approximation h_{a_n} -> f is with respect to the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
To make T_h(r) stand-alone, one should specify D(t) = {z in C : |z| < t}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The form omega in the characteristic is the Fubini-Study form on P^1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
Because the maps are entire on C, the growth question is asymptotic as r -> infinity. This is implicit in the paper’s formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

In the C-valued case, h^*(omega) is understood after viewing C as the standard affine chart in P^1; otherwise the pullback of the Fubini-Study form would be undefined. This is implicit rather than spelled out. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
For paper-faithful context, the paper notes that U is nonempty by Birkhoff’s theorem and in fact is a dense G_delta subset of H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Fix one of the two settings considered in the paper: either H = O(C,C), or H = O(C,P^1), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let U be the set of maps h in H such that for every f in H there exists a sequence (a_n) in C with h_{a_n}(z) := h(z+a_n) converging to f in H. Birkhoff’s theorem implies that U is nonempty. Determine the minimal possible asymptotic growth, as r -> infinity, of the Nevanlinna characteristic T_h(r) for h in U, where T_h(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(omega), D(t) = {z in C : |z| < t}, and omega is the Fubini-Study form on P^1 (with C viewed as the affine chart of P^1 in the C-valued case).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the least possible growth of T_h(r) as r -> infinity among those entire maps h whose translation orbit {z ↦ h(z+a) : a in C} is dense in H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: Section 9 introduces exactly the space H, the translation-universal set U, and then states Problem 9.1 in essentially the same words as your draft. The only refinements needed are to separate the two codomain cases exactly as the paper does, spell out the translate notation and compact-open convergence, and make explicit the asymptotic variable r -> infinity and the role of the Fubini-Study form. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
